summary.text: Karen Spalding is the Republican candidate for the Missouri House of Representatives, District 19, in the November 3, 2026 general election, where she faces incumbent Democrat Wick Thomas.
A longtime music teacher, Spalding previously ran for the seat in 2022 and 2024 and says she is running on lower and capped property taxes, school choice and education.

paragraphs.text: Karen Spalding graduated from Midway High School, attended Highland Community College, and earned a bachelor's degree from Washburn University in 1988.

In a Ballotpedia survey, Spalding said she graduated magna cum laude with a Bachelor of Music Education degree and has worked as a classroom, band and vocal teacher in Northeast Kansas public and private schools and later taught elementary music in Kansas City.
She described herself as an educator for 37 years, a widowed mother of four and grandmother of eight.
Spalding was the Republican candidate for Missouri House District 19 in 2022, losing to incumbent Ingrid Burnett, and again in 2024, losing to Wick Thomas.
In the survey, she said she is a member of the Jackson County Republican Committee and was chosen this year as president of the Missouri Association of Republicans.
Spalding advanced from the Republican primary on August 4, 2026.
In the survey, Spalding said she would work to lower taxes and cap property taxes, restrict foreign investors to support small businesses and support school choice.
She also said she supports closed borders and a path to legal status for responsible undocumented immigrants, and that only citizens with valid government identification should be able to vote.
